newsitem.title: USA: First Brands hurt by resin costs, low demand.
newsitem.headline: First Brands hurt by resin costs, low demand.

text.p: Higher resins costs and soft demand for consumer plastic wraps are dealing a one-two punch to First Brands Corp's earnings this quarter, a trend the company expects will continue into the next two quarters.

First Brands, the maker of Glad brand kitchen wrap, said Friday that analyst earnings estimates for the current fourth quarter ending June 30 and for the 1998 fiscal year were too high. Shares fell 3-3/4 to 22-1/4 in afternoon trading.
"Higher resin costs have been hurting their costs and crimping their margins," said Merrill Lynch housewares analyst John Gibbons. "There's not much they can do about higher resin costs."

Gibbons said resin costs were about 13 percent higher in the recent third fiscal quarter than the same quarter last year and up 30 percent this quarter versus a year ago. Resins are used to produce plastic for wraps and bags.

The higher costs kept First Brands' earnings flat at $0.39 per share last quarter, unchanged from the third quarter of the prior year. That performance was far short of a stated goal of 15-20 percent annual earnings growth, Gibbons said.

Gibbons said First Brands is also confronting slack consumer demand for plastic wraps, although it is holding its 28 percent market share amid competition from Tenneco Inc's Hefty and Dow Chemical Co's Saran brands.
Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette analyst Eileen Gormley said the soft demand suggested consumers had stocked up on plastic wraps.
"It looks like they've taken advantage of sales and coupons and aren't in any rush to restock the kitchen," she said.

Despite First Brands' current obstacles, Gormley said she was keeping her long-term buy rating on the company. "It will probably stabilize in the short term. They have good market share and are a good company," she said.

First Brands said problems were not limited to Glad. It said inventory reductions by retailers for its automotive products, including STP motor treatment, also contributed to earnings weakness. The company also cited above-average advertising and promotional expenses.
The company said it expects to be profitable in its fourth quarter, but said operating results may be $0.10 to $0.15 per share below year-earlier figures.
And it said operating results for the first half of fiscal year 1998 were likely to be slightly lower than in fiscal 1997 if market conditions failed to improve immediately.

One bright spot, First Brands said, was its line of pet products, including Scoop Away cat litter. But it cautioned profitability in the area would not offset weakness in the Glad and automotive markets.

First Call's consensus earnings estimate for the current fourth quarter was $0.48 per share, and for fiscal year 1998 was $1.95 per share before the company made its dampened earnings projections Friday morning.
The company said it expected its earnings would return to more normalized trends in the second half of fiscal 1998. First Brands' fiscal year begins July 1.
